newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA STRETCH LEAD OVER INDIA TO 290.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA STRETCH LEAD OVER INDIA TO 290.

text.p: Some solid batting from Andrew Hudson and Daryll Cullinan helped South Africa to stretch their overall lead over India to 290 at lunch on the fourth day of the second test in Cape Town on Sunday.
Hudson and Cullinan were both undefeated on 50 as the home side took their second innings score to 120 for three -- to add to their first innings lead of 170.

They lost only one wicket in the morning session when Lance Klusener, serving as nightwatchman after his first innings century batting at number nine, fell for 12, mispulling Javagal Srinath to Rahul Dravid at midwicket.
At 33 for three India may have entertained vague hopes of pulling off a victory to level the three-match series after their 328-run defeat in the first test in Durban.
But, although Hudson was dropped at midoff on 43 off leg-spinner Anil Kumble, the fourth wicket pair were untroubled on a Newlands wicket still heavily in favour of the batsmen.
Cullinan scored his second half-century of the match from 71 balls with six fours while Hudson took 114 deliveries and hit seven boundaries.
